title: Resilience, Redundancy, and Failure Domains
summary: Evaluate redundant paths and shared failure domains in a synthetic network.
objectives: Identify single points of failure and shared failure domains.
Evaluate how redundant links and devices affect simulated availability without promising zero downtime.

vocab.def: Additional components or paths that can support a service if one is unavailable.
A change to an alternate path or component after a condition is detected.

sections.heading: Prepare
sections.body: This exercise uses a synthetic topology. Learners do not perform live failover or maintenance.

sections.heading: Apply
sections.body: Compare two paths and list shared switches, power dependencies, and physical fiber routes. A second path improves options but does not remove every failure domain or guarantee uninterrupted service.

sections.heading: Prove
sections.body: State which failure domain is supported by the evidence and what should be escalated to an authorized operations team.

practice.prompt: Why might two links still share a failure domain?
practice.answer: They may share a switch, rack, power path, or physical fiber route.

quiz.question: What does redundancy provide?
options: Proof that every path is independent

reflectionPrompt: Which shared dependency limited the resilience claim?

careerConnection.text: This is supervised educational infrastructure practice, not professional qualification.
